title: Jetty WebSocket reserved opcode bypasses size checks and forces huge allocation
summary: With auto-fragmentation enabled, a reserved WebSocket opcode bypasses frame-size checks and clamps; Jetty allocates memory for the unvalidated attacker-declared payload before rejecting the opcode, enabling remote memory exhaustion.
ai_role: Anthropic CVD finding explicitly attributes discovery to Claude Mythos Preview; Jetty advisory identifies the individual GHSA and affected behavior.
classification_note: Public disclosure is documented. The cited accounts describe a remote unauthenticated denial-of-service condition; they do not establish exploitation in the wild or zero-day status. Anthropic says static analysis identified the bug and reports no attached reproducer.
remediation_note: The Jetty advisory lists patched releases 12.1.12, 12.0.38, 11.0.32, and 10.0.32.

impacts.conditions: A WebSocket frame with a reserved opcode; auto-fragmentation is on by default, allowing allocation before opcode rejection.
impacts.exploitation: The cited advisory does not state whether this issue was exploited in the wild.
